metadata.title: Matchscore
metadata.description: Match scoring app powered by Convex and Next.js

hero.badge: Automated social media for amateur football clubs
hero.title: Stay active on <highlight>social media</highlight> — without the extra work
hero.subtitle: Matchscore automatically posts match announcements and results to Facebook and Instagram, using your own club templates. More visibility for your team and sponsors, zero hassle.
hero.hint: Find your club and set up automated posts in minutes.

problem.title: Social media is essential — but who has the time?
problem.p1: Amateur football clubs in Belgium need a strong presence on social media. It builds a positive brand image, keeps supporters engaged, and shows sponsors their investment matters.
problem.p2: But it takes real effort: someone dedicated to taking photos, writing captions, and posting at the right moments — often after a long match day. Most clubs simply don't have that capacity.
problem.imageAlt: Amateur football match on a grass field

solution.title: Automated posts that look like you made them
solution.p1: Matchscore creates and publishes professional match visuals automatically — announcements before kick-off and results right after the final whistle. Your club's colours, your templates, your style.
solution.p2: Connect your calendar once, design a few templates, and turn on the automation. We handle the timing, the content, and the posting to Facebook and Instagram.

howItWorks.title: Three steps. Then it runs itself.
howItWorks.description: No technical skills needed. If you can upload an image and fill in a form, you're ready.

items.question: Do I need technical knowledge to use Matchscore?
items.answer: No. If you can upload an image and connect a social media account, you can use Matchscore. The setup wizard guides you through selecting your club, creating templates, and linking Facebook and Instagram.

items.question: How does the match calendar get imported?
items.answer: When you select your club, we automatically pull the first team's fixture list from the Belgian football federation. Based on that calendar, we know exactly when to post announcements and when to look for results.

items.question: Which social media platforms are supported?
items.answer: Matchscore currently supports Facebook and Instagram. You connect your club's accounts once during setup, and all automated posts are published directly to those channels.

items.question: Can I customise the visuals for my club?
items.answer: Absolutely. You create your own templates: upload a background image, position text fields, and add sponsor logos. For each post, we automatically fill in variables like the opponent name, score, match location, and team logos.

items.question: How are match results posted so quickly?
items.answer: We monitor the Belgian federation's results feed. As soon as your match result is published, Matchscore generates a result visual from your template and posts it to your connected social channels — no manual checking required.

items.question: Can I include our sponsors in posts?
items.answer: Yes. Add sponsor logos to your templates once, and they appear on every automated post. It's an easy way to deliver the social media visibility sponsors expect, without extra work each match week.

items.question: What if I want to pause or stop automations?
items.answer: You're always in control. You can turn individual automations on or off at any time from your dashboard. Pausing doesn't affect your templates or calendar — everything is ready when you want to resume.

items.question: Is the price per club or per team?
items.answer: Pricing is per club. One subscription covers your club's automations for the first team. All features are included in every plan — the only difference is the watermark on the Starter plan.

items.question: What happens after my yearly subscription ends?
items.answer: Your subscription renews annually. If you choose not to renew, automations stop but your templates and settings are saved. You can reactivate anytime by renewing your subscription.

items.question: Does our club need approval from the federation?
items.answer: Matchscore uses publicly available match data from the Belgian federation — the same information on their website. You're simply automating posts about your own club's matches using data that's already public.
